name: ps
summary: Shows a snapshot of running processes.
description: Lists processes at the moment it is called. ps accepts two syntaxes: BSD, without a dash (ps aux), and UNIX, with a dash (ps -ef). For a display that keeps refreshing, use top or htop.

options.description: Every process on the system (UNIX syntax). -A is the same.

example.output:
PID TTY          TIME CMD
      1 ?        00:00:02 systemd
      2 ?        00:00:00 kthreadd

options.description: Full format: UID, PID, PPID (parent process), start time, full command.
Columns to show, for example -o pid,user,%cpu,cmd.
Sorts by a column; a “-” in front reverses the order (--sort=-%mem).
Shows the tree of parent and child processes.

arguments.name: aux
arguments.description: BSD syntax: a (all users), u (user-oriented format, with %CPU and %MEM), x (including processes without a terminal).

examples.explanation: Every process with CPU and memory usage.
examples.output:
USER    PID %CPU %MEM    VSZ   RSS TTY  STAT START TIME COMMAND
root      1  0.0  0.1 167588 11808 ?    Ss   09:12 0:02 /sbin/init

examples.explanation: The processes using the most memory.
The processes of the user esprit.
